# zag workbench

> A standards-native, Zig-native workbench where people and agents do engineering work in one recorded workspace.

Everything that happens becomes a typed event in a hash-chained log with content-addressed command output, a read-only object audit and evidence-preserving recovery. Agents propose typed tool requests; a local policy engine decides them. Terminology, metadata, accessibility, data quality and AI governance are enforced by the build, not described in a document.

- [README](/README.md): What the workbench is and how to build it

- [Roadmap](/docs/roadmap.md): What is complete, what comes next and how completion will be proved
- [Threat model](/docs/threat-model.md): Trust boundaries, implemented controls and residual security work
- [Platform support](/docs/platform-support.md): Compile evidence, runtime evidence and explicit platform exclusions
- [Contributing](/CONTRIBUTING.md): How to prepare and check a change
- [Security policy](/SECURITY.md): How to report a vulnerability privately
- [Plain language](/docs/plain-language.md): How ISO 24495 is applied to product text, and what the checker cannot decide
- [Glossary](/docs/glossary.md): The registered concepts and their definitions
- [Competitive position](/docs/competitive-position.md): What zag does that other terminals do not, what it cannot do yet, and the order that changes
